This isn’t about claiming we have better cybersecurity than the companies building AI agents. It’s about how the systems are designed. Your agent decides what it wants to do. Clam checks those requests against your rules. Your agent can’t change those rules through Clam.

## Your inbox stays yours

Clam isn’t another place where your email lives. We don’t keep a copy of your mailbox, and we never give your agents your email credentials.

Clam starts with Gmail, with more email providers planned. Learn more in Privacy and security.

## Ready to give your agent some freedom?

Start small, with receipts or the emails you’ve been missing, then give your agent more responsibility one permission at a time.

Quickstart: connect your first agent in about 10 minutes. [...] 1. Allowed: your agent gets to work, with no interruption.
2. Needs your approval: Clam asks you, and your agent continues only if you approve.
3. Denied: Clam blocks it.

Your Audit log shows what your agents tried, what went through and what was blocked.

## Why should I trust Clam with my email?

If you’re worried about giving Claude, Muse or another AI agent your inbox, why give it to Clam instead? Because Clam was built to do something fundamentally different.

Your AI agent is designed to be autonomous. It makes decisions, plans its next steps and uses tools to reach your goals. That’s what makes it useful, and it’s why a cleverly written email can sway it. [...] Get started

# What is Clam?

Clam lets your AI agents work autonomously with your email, while you stay in control of what they can see and do.

Imagine waking up to an inbox that’s already been taken care of. Your agent has found yesterday’s receipts and the five updates from your daughter’s school, archived the promotions and drafted replies to the messages that need you. All while you were having your morning workout.

With the right rules, it can do all that without access to your bank statements or conversations with your therapist. And it can ask for your approval before forwarding an email.

results.title: AI Agents for Email Management: Automate Your Inbox
results.content:
## Final Thoughts

Start with what you already pay for. Turn on Gmail's free AI features, or Outlook's if your company has Copilot, and use them for a week.

Then name the problem honestly. If it is your own inbox, try one dedicated AI email agent on a free plan or trial. If it is a shared mailbox that should feed a CRM, a ticket queue or a finance system, build a small workflow in an agent builder instead.

Whichever you choose, keep it on drafts until it has handled your real senders for a couple of weeks without a bad call. Then let it send only the messages it has proved it can handle, and keep a human on everything else.

## Frequently Asked Questions [...] Until that settles, your own two-week trial is a better guide than any star rating.

Underneath all four sits the risk every vendor here designs around: an agent sending the wrong reply to the wrong person. A wrong label costs you a minute. A confident, wrong reply to a client, a regulator or your manager costs a great deal more, which is why drafting for review, not sending, is still the default even among the most aggressive products.

## AI Agents for Email Management in Practice: Three Situations

Most readers fall into one of two situations: the inbox itself is the problem, or the inbox is the front door to a process that lives somewhere else. The first points to a dedicated AI email agent. The second points to a general agent with email as one of its tools. [...] What follows names the tools in each group, with prices taken from their own pages and dated, and says what each one automates. It also covers where a human still has to stay in the loop, and gives a short checklist for adopting one. A disclosure first: we build Orchestra, a control plane for running AI agents and data pipelines, so we sell into the wider agent space.

None of the inbox tools below compete with us, and where they are worth paying for, we say so.

## The Short Answer

What it is. Software that reads your email, sorts it, drafts replies or sends them, with little or no manual step from you. The serious products all do some mix of triage and drafting.

Very few send on your behalf without asking first.
